speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast tumor (superior sulcus tumor) causing right brachial plexus compression.

Given your history of smoking and significant weight loss, combined with the progressive weakness and sensory loss in the right arm, this clinical picture strongly suggests a lung malignancy in the apex compressing the brachial plexus. I will need to confirm this with imaging immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray and CT_Chest.
